title: AMDA and The Gauchers Association: a first conversation about shared registries

sentences.text: At AMDA, we support Pompe families; The Gauchers Association supports Gaucher families.
Both diseases involve missing enzyme activity and material building up inside lysosomes, the cell’s recycling compartments.
This shared biology offers a reason to explore collaboration, not proof that the same approaches will work.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The Registry of Patients Diagnosed With Lysosomal Storage Diseases and A Global Prospective Observational Registry of Patients With Pompe Disease already include Pompe.
The AMDA Research Grant is another existing Pompe resource.
We could exchange information about these resources without assuming access, funding or suitability for Gaucher.
The Institutional Registry of Rare Diseases includes Gaucher and offers a concrete starting point for an inquiry.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Pompe involves glycogen buildup in muscle, while Gaucher involves glucosylceramide buildup mainly in immune cells called macrophages.

Please help check whether difficulty descending stairs, reduced muscle alpha-1,4-glucosidase activity and elevated urine glucose tetrasaccharide also occur in Gaucher, rather than treating missing records as absence.
We should also check variant-specific responses to protein-stabilizing compounds before drawing parallels.
The atlas’s splice-variant loss-of-function links are inferred, unverified and below 0.5 confidence; the Gaucher protein-misfolding connection carries contested evidence.
Send one inquiry to The Gauchers Association asking whether the Institutional Registry of Rare Diseases could include Pompe and who could confirm eligibility.

Which variants in GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA are “amenable”—responsive to a protein-stabilizing chaperone—as GLA variants are classified for migalastat in published evidence to discuss with a neurologist?
Could a cross-gene table of laboratory responses distinguish actual responsiveness from genetic consequence labels and test the proposed connection to SLC6A1?
Dear The Gauchers Association team,
I’m writing on behalf of AMDA to explore a small collaboration.
Pompe and Gaucher share lysosomal storage biology.
Could you help us ask whether the Institutional Registry of Rare Diseases could include Pompe?
We would welcome your guidance before taking this further.
[Your name], on behalf of Acid Maltase Deficiency Association (AMDA)
